overall_basis: The frozen Acts candidate is mechanically exact and preserves the formal mesh, but all 110 LOW-confidence decisions remain candidate-only holds. Each decision carries three MATERIAL formal challenges, one unresolved append-only appeal, at least one bounded MATERIAL peer-family challenge, and a required author response. This same-model, shared-substrate peer crosscheck is not an independent cross-model vote and cannot force consensus.

material_peer_challenges.claim: Test whether the preface, commission, replacement scene, Pentecost event, speech, response, and community summary remain distinguishable but not mechanically detached.
material_peer_challenges.risk: Authorship, source, Pentecost doctrine, or citation fulfillment could silently replace literary boundary evidence.
material_peer_challenges.required_author_response: Defend each proposed seam from Acts.1.1 through Acts.2.47 using explicit scene, speech-frame, response, and closure evidence; address every preserved larger and smaller alternative without invoking authorship, source, witness choice, or doctrine.
material_peer_challenges.preserved_alternatives: All exact alternatives in the three blind proposals, three formal primaries, candidate rows, and append-only appeal ledger remain unresolved.

material_peer_challenges.claim: Test the sign-speech-response-arrest-hearing-prayer sequence as a linked movement while preserving defensible internal seams.
material_peer_challenges.risk: The healing, speech, audience response, arrest, hearing, or prayer may be detached by chapter or topic, or fused by miracle/legal/theological assumptions.
material_peer_challenges.required_author_response: Explain the literary evidence for each seam across Acts.3.1-Acts.4.31 and show how occasion, speech, response, arrest, hearing, release, and prayer frames are retained; do not rely on miracle claims, Roman or Jewish law, or theology.
material_peer_challenges.preserved_alternatives: All exact alternatives in the three blind proposals, three formal primaries, candidate rows, and append-only appeal ledger remain unresolved.

material_peer_challenges.claim: Test the relation among community summary, Barnabas example, Ananias and Sapphira counterexample, signs summary, hearing, and renewed public witness.
material_peer_challenges.risk: Summary/example/counterexample units may be over-split or fused into an ideal-community, institutional, economic, ethical, or doctrinal conclusion.
material_peer_challenges.required_author_response: Defend summary-to-example, counterexample, signs, arrest, hearing, and closure seams with literary evidence and answer all exact alternatives without idealizing the community or authorizing institutional, economic, ethical, or theological claims.
material_peer_challenges.preserved_alternatives: All exact alternatives in the three blind proposals, three formal primaries, candidate rows, and append-only appeal ledger remain unresolved.

material_peer_challenges.claim: Test the appointment, Stephen controversy, accusation, hearing, long speech, hostile response, and death as complete framed movements with explicit internal speech structure.
material_peer_challenges.risk: The Stephen speech may be atomized at citations or flattened into one block, and historical chronology, collective guilt, or theology may be treated as boundary authority.
material_peer_challenges.required_author_response: Account for the appointment and Stephen transition, the speech frame and major rhetorical movements, and the Acts.7.53/7.54 response seam; preserve exact alternatives and avoid historical reconstruction, collective-guilt inference, or doctrinal adjudication.
material_peer_challenges.preserved_alternatives: All exact alternatives in the three blind proposals, three formal primaries, candidate rows, and append-only appeal ledger remain unresolved.

material_peer_challenges.claim: Test scattering, Samaria, Simon, angelic direction, encounter with the official, interpretation, baptism, and onward travel as related but separately framed scenes.
material_peer_challenges.risk: Narrative scenes may be joined or divided by identity, baptismal, pneumatological, mission, or harmonization claims; Acts.8.37 may be used as selected textual evidence.
material_peer_challenges.required_author_response: Defend scene, participant, location, question-answer, interpretation, baptism, and travel seams; keep Acts.8.37 and all identity, history, witness, and theological questions evidence-only and deferred.
material_peer_challenges.preserved_alternatives: All exact alternatives in the three blind proposals, three formal primaries, candidate rows, and append-only appeal ledger remain unresolved.

material_peer_challenges.claim: Test the repeated Saul encounter reports, Peter healing cycle, and Cornelius-Peter paired visions, meeting, speech, response, and Jerusalem report without forced harmonization.
material_peer_challenges.risk: Repeated accounts and paired visions may be fused as identical event reports or split by theological motifs; food, Gentile inclusion, source, identity, or chronology claims may decide boundaries.
material_peer_challenges.required_author_response: Trace scene and report frames for Saul, Peter, and Cornelius, distinguish event, retelling, vision, meeting, speech, response, and report, and answer alternatives without harmonization, source claims, identity claims, chronology, or food/Gentile theology.
material_peer_challenges.preserved_alternatives: All exact alternatives in the three blind proposals, three formal primaries, candidate rows, and append-only appeal ledger remain unresolved.

material_peer_challenges.claim: Test the Antioch emergence, Barnabas-Saul ministry, famine relief, Herod persecution, release, judgment, and return as a bounded narrative complex.
material_peer_challenges.risk: Mission, famine, persecution, release, and return may be joined by reconstructed chronology or detached by topic; Acts.11.20 and Acts.12.25 textual questions may be treated as selected readings.
material_peer_challenges.required_author_response: Defend Antioch, famine-relief, Herod, release, judgment, and return seams from narrative and travel frames; keep chronology, identity, historicity, and Acts.11.20/12.25 readings unresolved.
material_peer_challenges.preserved_alternatives: All exact alternatives in the three blind proposals, three formal primaries, candidate rows, and append-only appeal ledger remain unresolved.

material_peer_challenges.claim: Test the sending, itinerary, synagogue and public speeches, audience responses, conflict, returns, appointments, and Antioch report as complete mission movements.
material_peer_challenges.risk: Speeches may be detached from occasions and responses or travel compressed by theology, fulfillment, civic history, or reconstructed chronology.
material_peer_challenges.required_author_response: Defend each speech-travel-response seam across Acts.13-14, retain complete occasions and responses, and address citation and textual alternatives without authorizing fulfillment, theology, civic history, chronology, or witness choice.
material_peer_challenges.preserved_alternatives: All exact alternatives in the three blind proposals, three formal primaries, candidate rows, and append-only appeal ledger remain unresolved.

material_peer_challenges.claim: Test dispute, journey, assembly, speeches, discernment, letter frame, delegation, delivery, response, and Antioch teaching as a complete council-letter movement.
material_peer_challenges.risk: Speeches or the letter may be detached, fused, or treated as institutional/doctrinal legislation; textual variants or Galatians chronology may determine boundaries.
material_peer_challenges.required_author_response: Explain dispute, assembly, speaker, letter, delegation, delivery, response, and closure seams; preserve exact alternatives and defer witness selection, institutional authority, doctrine, and Galatians chronology.
material_peer_challenges.preserved_alternatives: All exact alternatives in the three blind proposals, three formal primaries, candidate rows, and append-only appeal ledger remain unresolved.

material_peer_challenges.claim: Test the team separation, Timothy encounter, travel prohibitions, Macedonian vision and response, first-person-plural shift, Lydia household, imprisonment, jailer household, and release.
material_peer_challenges.risk: Travel, vision, household, prison, and legal scenes may be split by doctrinal or biographical inference; Acts.16.7 and the we-shift may be used to prove reading, authorship, source, or eyewitness status.
material_peer_challenges.required_author_response: Defend team, travel, vision-response, household, imprisonment, baptism, magistrate, and release seams; treat Acts.16.7 and Acts.16.10-16.17 first-person plural only as deferred textual/narrative evidence.
material_peer_challenges.preserved_alternatives: All exact alternatives in the three blind proposals, three formal primaries, candidate rows, and append-only appeal ledger remain unresolved.

material_peer_challenges.claim: Test the Thessalonica, Berea, Athens, Corinth, Gallio, and return-travel movements with speeches and audience responses intact.
material_peer_challenges.risk: The Athens speech may be atomized at embedded sayings or detached from response, while epistle relations, civic history, philosophy, or Gallio chronology may authorize seams.
material_peer_challenges.required_author_response: Defend location, participant, speech, response, hearing, and travel seams across Acts.17.1-18.23; preserve embedded-saying and textual alternatives without epistle alignment, philosophical judgment, civic reconstruction, or chronology as boundary authority.
material_peer_challenges.preserved_alternatives: All exact alternatives in the three blind proposals, three formal primaries, candidate rows, and append-only appeal ledger remain unresolved.

material_peer_challenges.claim: Test Apollos, Ephesus disciples, synagogue and hall ministry, extraordinary deeds, Sceva episode, renunciation, travel intention, and riot as separately framed but related movements.
material_peer_challenges.risk: Teaching, spirit, magic, economy, civic assembly, or theology may dictate units; Acts.19.40 and other variants may be silently selected.
material_peer_challenges.required_author_response: Defend participant, teaching, location, episode, summary, intention, riot, speech, and dismissal seams; keep magical, pneumatological, civic, economic, theological, and Acts.19.40 textual judgments non-authorizing.
material_peer_challenges.preserved_alternatives: All exact alternatives in the three blind proposals, three formal primaries, candidate rows, and append-only appeal ledger remain unresolved.

material_peer_challenges.claim: Test return travel, companion list, first-person-plural itinerary, Troas gathering/Eutychus episode, onward voyage, Miletus summons, farewell speech, response, and departure.
material_peer_challenges.risk: Lists, itinerary, miracle, farewell discourse, and leadership vocabulary may be over-split or used for authorship, eyewitness, polity, or doctrine; Acts.20.15/20.28 may be selected.
material_peer_challenges.required_author_response: Defend list, travel, gathering, episode, voyage, summons, speech, response, and departure seams; keep we-shifts, Acts.20.15/20.28, authorship, eyewitness status, polity, and doctrine evidence-only.
material_peer_challenges.preserved_alternatives: All exact alternatives in the three blind proposals, three formal primaries, candidate rows, and append-only appeal ledger remain unresolved.

material_peer_challenges.claim: Test the Jerusalem journey and warnings, arrival meeting, temple action, arrest, crowd defense, citizenship exchange, council defense, plot, escort, and official letter.
material_peer_challenges.risk: Warnings, speeches, legal scenes, or chapter crossings may be fragmented; historicity, Roman law, collective guilt, theology, or we-shift evidence may decide seams.
material_peer_challenges.required_author_response: Account for journey, warning, meeting, arrest, speech-frame crossings at Acts.21.40/22.1 and Acts.22.30/23.1, council, plot, letter, and transfer; defer legal, historical, collective-guilt, theological, textual, and authorship judgments.
material_peer_challenges.preserved_alternatives: All exact alternatives in the three blind proposals, three formal primaries, candidate rows, and append-only appeal ledger remain unresolved.

material_peer_challenges.claim: Test the successive Felix, Festus, and Agrippa hearings, delays, appeal, consultation, defense, repeated encounter report, response, and verdict.

material_peer_challenges.required_author_response: Defend accusation, defense, adjournment, succession, appeal, consultation, Agrippa address, response, and verdict seams; preserve repeated-account alternatives without harmonization, Roman-law conclusions, innocence claims, chronology, or witness selection.
